BiblicalUsage: To desolate is to strip a land bare, and it is the word for God's judgment on cities and kingdoms. God destroyed the Amorite before Israel, Jehu destroyed Baal out of Israel, and Moses heard the LORD say, let Me alone, that I may destroy them and blot out their name. Isaiah sees the day of the LORD coming to lay the land desolate and destroy the sinners out of it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God destroys what He cannot cleanse, and the desolation of a land is the last word when its people will not repent. The Amorite, Baal, and the sinners of Isaiah's day all met the same end, and that is why I take His warnings as promises.
